To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
epithelial cells secrete a series of factors that attract and direct neutrophils to the site of infection in the intestine.

1) the epithelial cell is the first line of defense against pathogenic invasion, 2) the epithelial barrier is a dynamic structure that changes in response to the presence of pathogens, 3) the epithelial cells are the first line of the host immune system, 4) the epithelial immune response is coordinated by a series of secreted products, 5) the epithelial secretory products are directed to the site of infection by a process of polarized secretion, and
1) Epithelial cells are capable of directional secretion of chemokines that control neutrophil recruitment to the intestine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which the intestinal mucosa controls the migration of neutrophils into the intestine during inflammation.
understanding the mechanisms of epithelial cell control of neutrophil migration at mucosal surfaces.
the mechanisms of neutrophil trafficking to the intestinal epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epithelial cells are the first and most important line of defense of the host.
the epithelium has an important role in the regulation of the immune response to pathogens at mucosal surfaces.
neutrophils are the first line of defense in the innate immune response against invading pathogens and epithelial cells are the first to recognize and react to invading bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epithelial cells control the direction and magnitude of the innate immune response at mucosal surfaces by secreting a variety of factors in a coordinated manner.

epithelial cells control the migration and activity of neutrophils at mucosal surfaces through the directional secretion of a variety of products that act at different stages of the inflammatory cascade.
epithelial cells are not passive barriers but rather active participants that regulate the immune response to microbes at mucosal surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epithelial cells can direct neutrophil migration at mucosal surfaces via the secretion of specific factors that are differentially regulated by the presence of bacteria.
the epithelial cell is not simply a passive barrier, but an integral part of the immune system.
epithelial cells can direct the movement of neutrophils by releasing a combination of chemokines and other secreted products that are specifically designed to attract and activate neutrophils.
